help.title: Phonics Hunt
help.intro: A two-team learning game where teams take turns opening word tiles and finding hidden stars. The product name is Phonics Hunt.
help.usage1: Enter words and set team names, star count, and star points.
help.usage2: Press Start Game to create tiles automatically based on the word count.
help.usage3: Each tile shows its word from the start; stars are hidden randomly in the set number of tiles.
help.usage4: Press the Blue Team or Red Team turn button, then open the tile matching the word the student says.
help.usage5: Opening a star tile adds points to that team.
help.usage6: When all tiles are opened, the game ends and scores are compared.
help.inputLine1: Enter one word per line (press Enter after each line). At least 2 words are required.
help.notes: Star count can be set from 1 up to the number of words entered. Reset Scores clears points only; Edit Words returns to the setup screen.

help.title: Castle Siege
help.intro: A battle activity where two teams attack, repair, and defend castle HP across lesson rounds.
help.usage1: On the setup screen, set team names, castle HP, homework bonus, and lesson rounds.
help.usage2: Press Start Battle to enter the battle screen.
help.usage3: Use Attack, Repair, Shield, and Charge under each team.
help.usage4: Attack reduces the opponent's castle HP; Repair restores your team's HP.
help.usage5: Shield builds defense; Charge lets a team act twice on the next turn.
help.usage6: When an opponent's castle HP reaches 0, that team wins the round. End Round advances to the next round.
help.usage7: After the final round, the lesson is complete.
help.prep4: Available items: Shield, Repair Kit, Charge
help.notes: Attack damage and Shield values are randomized within set ranges. Charge lets the same team act twice in a row.

winner.subtitleDraw: Both fortresses fell at the same time!

help.title: Fortress Battle
help.intro: A turn-based classroom battle where Team A and Team B attack each other's fortress HP.
help.usage1: Set starting HP and damage values in Game Settings, then press Apply.
help.usage2: Switch turns with Team A Turn / Team B Turn.
help.usage3: Choose Attack 1–4 to deal damage based on your configured values.
help.usage4: When a fortress reaches 0 HP, the other team wins.
help.notes: Damage values are comma-separated numbers (e.g. 0,10,20,30). A value of 0 shows MISS!

help.title: Pirate Race
help.intro: A race game where two teams move pirate ships toward the goal.
help.usage1: Adjust goal distance, Storm Mode, and Treasure Bonus settings.
help.usage2: Select move values +1 through +6 or use Random Move.
help.usage3: The first team to reach the goal wins.
help.notes: This is not turn-enforced — the teacher manages play order.

status.newMapReady: New map ready — select a team to excavate

toast.groundShift: ⛏ The ground shifts! Hidden tiles reshuffled!

help.title: Treasure Hunt
help.intro: A two-team activity where players dig tiles to collect treasure points.
help.usage1: Select Blue Team or Red Team Excavate to choose the active team.
help.usage2: Pick a tile to dig and reveal its contents.
help.usage3: Treasures (⭐, 💎, 👑) add points to that team.
help.usage4: When all tiles are dug, the game ends and scores are compared.
help.usage5: Change grid size with Rows/Cols and press New Map for a fresh board.
help.usage6: Reset Game clears scores and starts over.
help.special1: 🗺 Treasure Map: briefly shows one undug treasure location.
help.special2: 💣 Dynamite: the same team picks one more tile.
help.special3: ⛏ Unstable Ground: reshuffles undug tile contents.
help.notes: Grid size ranges from 3–8 rows and 3–8 columns. Treasure points: ⭐ 1, 💎 2, 👑 3.

help.title: Tug of War
help.intro: A tug-of-war game where the rope moves based on the score difference between two teams.
help.usage1: Set team names and the win point target.
help.usage3: Enter scores for Team A and Team B.
help.usage4: Press Pull to move the rope.
help.usage5: The first team to reach the win point target wins.
help.inputLine1: Enter scores as numbers. Press Enter to pull.
help.notes: Scores are entered directly as numbers (0–9), not drawn from cards.
